The ORIGINAL script drew Poisson(7) and deleted subjects outside 4-12, drawing replacements until 500 survived - so the analysed count distribution was Poisson(7) conditioned on [4,12] and the stated n = 500 is correct. The revision KEEPS the floor of 4 and DROPS the ceiling. A floor has a real justification: predicted_yhat() cannot fit a singleton, and very sparse subjects are unstable. A ceiling has none - discarding well-observed subjects only throws information away. Counts are REDRAWN rather than clamped, so the retained distribution is a genuine truncated Poisson rather than a spike at the floor. LIMITATION TO STATE: with a floor of 4 the design never tests subjects with 2 or 3 observations, which is arguably the sparse regime the title refers to.

note: components RETAINED when fitting, as distinct from M_true = 2. Briefly set to 4 on 2026-09-05 because cumulative FVE >= 0.90 on the ROBUST spectrum selects 4 on all twelve arm x d cells. REVERTED THE SAME DAY: measured, 4 is worse on every axis. M1 aRI falls MONOTONICALLY in nK_fit - 0.968 / 0.937 / 0.719 on arm 1 at d = 3, and 0.945 / 0.868 / 0.608 on arm 4 at d = 1.5 - while cost rises 13x and the loop becomes CAP-BOUND, iter = 100 of maxIter = 100 on both cells. A cap-bound fit is an artefact of where the loop was cut off and is unreportable, and 4 is already past the convergence ceiling. nK_fit = 3 already cycles on both arms. M2 collapses to 0.127 on arm 1 at nK = 4. THE FVE RULE AND THE CONVERGENCE EVIDENCE DISAGREE - report the disagreement rather than leading with FVE, since FVE says how much variance four components capture, not that the loop can fit them. The components row of the settings block explores 1 to 4 and the FVE thresholds; that is where this gets written up. CONFIRMED 2026-09-06 on the decisions block, factor nkfit, 20 replicates at n = 500, and the reversal stands unchanged. nK = 4 is CAP-BOUND ON EVERY SINGLE FIT - conv 0.00 with iter 100 of 100 on BOTH arms, 40 of 40 fits - so its accuracy figures are not accuracy at all but an artefact of where the loop was cut off, and must never be quoted as though nK = 4 merely fits worse. Against nK = 3 the choice is decided on arm 1, where 0.972 beats 0.876 by 0.096 against twice the larger MCSE of 0.023; on arm 4 the two are 0.278 and 0.403 with MCSEs near 0.2 and CANNOT be ranked, so the arm that settles this is the Gaussian one. Cost at nK = 4 is 13x and reconstruction error on arm 1 rises from 0.023 to 2.166.

1.5, CONFIRMED by measurement. Gaussian arm, n = 200, 5 reps: RKCFC 0.985 [0.965, 0.995] against KCFC 0.955 [0.590, 0.980] - the methods separate and KCFC is unstable. The moment ladder also differentiates here: RKCFC falls to 0.658 on the t nu = 1.5 arm, so this separation is not too easy. NOTE the classes also differ in EIGENFUNCTIONS (sines against cosines), which alone gives RKCFC 0.925 at d = 0, so d controls only part of the separation and never had much room.

2, NOT 3. WAS 3 until 2026-09-05; the design is easy at that d, giving Delta 4.2-5.3 at d = 3. d = 3 IS SATURATED at n = 500: on the Gaussian arm M1 and M2 both returned aRI 0.968, identical to three decimals, so the two methods cannot be ranked there - the same defect the submitted design had at d = 5, one rung lower. The Delta sweep (6 arms x d in 0,1,1.5,2,2.5,3,4, 3 reps) puts d = 2 at median Delta 3.20, reference CCR 0.945, inside the discriminating band; d = 3 sits at 4.61 in the strong band near saturation. The pair {1.5, 2} therefore spans Delta 2.05 to 3.20. Confirm with an accuracy run before reporting: Delta places the level, it does not prove the methods separate there. CONFIRMED 2026-09-06 on the decisions block, factor d, 20 replicates at n = 500, levels 0 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 PAIRED on a common seed: on arm 4 at d = 2 the methods are 0.925 against 0.003, a gap of 0.922 against twice the larger bootstrap MCSE of 0.146, which is the widest separation of any level tested. d = 3 is where M2 RECOVERS, to 0.358 - so retiring it was right, but NOT for the saturation reason recorded above: on arm 1 at d = 3 the two are 0.984 and 0.960, indistinguishable, while on arm 4 they are pulling apart again. The level was retired on the arm where it saturates and it is the OTHER arm that justifies the retirement. d = 0 also earns its place: arm 1 scores 0.945 there, so the eigenfunction difference alone carries most of the separation and d never had much room, exactly as the d_hard note says.

convergence when the reclassification proportion reaches zero. With conv_prop = 0 the convergence test is an exact partition match, so it also detects cycles; RKCFC() reports which of the two happened via stop_reason. CONFIRMED 2026-09-06 on the HPC decisions block, factor convprop, 20 replicates at n = 500, thresholds 0 / 0.001 / 0.005 / 0.01 each scored by agree_strict against the cp = 0 partition OF THE SAME REPLICATE. agree is 1.000 in every cell of both arms bar one (0.995), so relaxing the threshold does not change the ANSWER anywhere - the reported non-convergence is COSMETIC, a few boundary subjects oscillating while the partition itself settled long before. Note also that relaxing cp does NOT buy convergence: M1 on arm 4 sits at 0.70 at all four thresholds. Keep 0 and report the non-convergence honestly rather than tuning it away, which is what the agree column exists to license.

k-means start with a random fallback when a class has fewer than 10 curves, which is exactly the condition that would otherwise make the fit be refused. The initialisation row of the settings block varies this deliberately. CONFIRMED 2026-09-06 on the HPC decisions block, factor init, 20 replicates at n = 500, and THE FALLBACK IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THIS SETTING. Stripping it - which is what the kendall_kmeans level does - fails on 16 of 20 arm-4 replicates with exactly that small-cluster refusal; Ward fails 19 of 20 and k-means on PACE scores 18 of 20, while random restarts and the oracle start fail NONE. Under infinite variance the initialiser is the failure point, not the algorithm: any start derived by clustering heavy-tailed scores puts the outliers in a cluster of their own. Two further findings. First, random20 MATCHES THE ORACLE (0.880 against 0.876 on arm 4; 0.972 against 0.976 on arm 1, both inside twice the MCSE), so restarts already buy everything a perfect start could and no change of initialiser is warranted. Second, oracle convergence on arm 4 is only 0.70 - starting from the TRUE labels, three fits in ten still do not converge - so arm-4 non-convergence is not an initialisation problem at all. NOTE the 2026-09-06 run omitted two-staged itself as a level, so its own numbers had to be borrowed from the nkfit/d/convprop baselines, which are seeded differently and therefore unpaired; the level has since been added to both run_settings.R and run_decisions.R.

replicates for the core grid; Monte Carlo error scales as 1/sqrt(B). PRICED 2026-09-06 AND THE COUNT IS NOT THE PROBLEM - THE SUMMARY STATISTIC IS. The decisions block measured one cell three times by accident: arm 4 / M1 / nK 2 / d_hard / cp 0 is the baseline of the nkfit, d and convprop factors alike, differing only in a scenario_id string that reseeds the data. Three independent sets of 20 replicates returned medians 0.278, 0.891 and 0.865. The per-replicate values explain it completely - the cell is BIMODAL, with mass at exactly 0 and mass at 0.85 to 0.95 and almost nothing between, and success fractions of 0.45, 0.65 and 0.65. Because that straddles one half, THE MEDIAN JUMPS DISCONTINUOUSLY BETWEEN THE TWO MODES and 0.278 is simply the median landing in the empty gap. Subsampling the pooled 60 draws (R/diag_stability.R) puts the median's 90 percent interval at width 0.61 for B = 50, 0.35 for B = 100 and still 0.14 for B = 500, against P(success) at 0.24, 0.16 and 0.07. 1/sqrt(B) is not wrong; the per-replicate variance is simply enormous on a two-point distribution. KEEP B = 100 AND REPORT ARM 4 AS P(success) PLUS THE CONDITIONAL MEDIAN GIVEN SUCCESS. The headline contrast is safe either way - M2 succeeds on about 2 percent of arm-4 replicates against M1's 58 - but M1's own arm-4 performance has no single typical value to quote.
